idea-plugin.name: Doppler Secrets Manager (Unofficial)
idea-plugin.description:
Browse, edit, and synchronize your Doppler secrets, and inject them into Run and Debug launches without leaving your IDE.

Unofficial, independently developed plugin. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Doppler. Doppler's name and trademarks belong to Doppler Technologies, Inc. The plugin uses an original icon.

Features

  • Browse secrets — explore projects, environments, and configs in the Doppler tool window. Empty config lists show an explanation that the project may be empty or access may be restricted. Empty and error branches collapse after five seconds and can be expanded again.
  • Edit as YAML — open a config in an editor tab, including multiline values and restricted-secret placeholders.
  • Save to synchronize — saving pushes a minimal set of changes to Doppler. Saves check for conflicting remote edits and apply replacements before deletions; rejected writes leave your editor changes available for correction. Reload or use automatic refresh to retrieve remote changes.
  • Secret-reference completion — get completion suggestions for Doppler secret references while editing.
  • Folder Setup — choose the default Doppler project and config for your IDE project, including inherited folder defaults. A bookmark marks the selected config in the tree and editor tabs; background checks reflect changes made through the CLI. When no configs are visible, Settings explains that the project may be empty or access may be restricted and disables config selection.
  • Folder-scoped authentication — use the current IDE project folder's Doppler login for browsing, editing, completion, and folder setup, without replacing the global login. Account validation and caches respect the IDE project context.
  • Test Connection — check CLI availability, account and workplace identity, and CLI version using the current IDE project folder's scope. Settings opened without a project checks the global login. A successful check confirms authentication; it does not verify access to projects, configs, or secrets, or validate the folder's selected project and config.
  • Setup guidance — detect a missing CLI or login and offer installation and authentication commands in Terminal. Supported systems use package-manager commands; the fallback installer can be reviewed before choosing per-user or system installation, with a checksum check that the reviewed script has not changed before execution.
  • CLI updates — manually check for the latest stable Doppler CLI release or enable automatic checks once per IDE/plugin startup, including at the welcome screen. Automatic checks are enabled by default and can be disabled in Settings. Updates require confirmation and run doppler update without elevation; package-manager installations may require their original package manager instead.
  • Run and Debug injection — automatically load the default config into Java, Python, Node.js and npm, Maven, Gradle, and Docker launch environments, including Docker images, Dockerfiles, and Compose. Each launch fetches fresh secrets; explicit run configuration variables take precedence.
  • Secret name transformers and custom mappings — control injected names from the default Doppler project/config selected in Folder Setup. Keep original names with none (the default), or use Doppler's camel, upper-camel, lower-snake, tf-var, dotnet-env, or lower-kebab transformer. Choose custom to rename selected secrets, for example API_KEY to APP_API_KEY, while leaving unmapped names unchanged. Settings are per IDE project and affect only Run and Debug injection, never names or values stored in Doppler. Invalid mappings or renames that overwrite another injected secret stop the launch.
  • Runnable injection examples — try Java, Maven, Python, Node.js/npm, Gradle, Docker image/Dockerfile, and Docker Compose checks with synthetic values and custom mappings. The examples guide covers setup and cleanup without printing environment values.
  • CLI diagnostics — optionally log sanitized command metadata, durations, and exit status, without secret values or CLI output.

Run and Debug setup

Open Settings → Tools → Doppler, use Folder Setup to select your defaults, then enable injection on the Run and Debug page. Injection starts disabled and requires approval for each project in this IDE; workspace files alone cannot enable it.

Run and Debug controls stay inactive until Folder Setup has both a default project and config. Saving or clearing those defaults updates the controls while Settings is open; saved injection preferences and custom mappings are preserved.

For Docker Compose, reference the injected variables in your Compose file to pass them to services. Custom mappings do not rewrite Compose keys or references; declare the mapped names explicitly and recreate containers after changing their environment. Running applications and containers keep their inherited environment for their lifetime; secret changes apply to the next launch.

Secret handling

Opened secret documents are held in memory rather than saved as local project files. Secret values being saved are passed to the Doppler CLI through standard input, not command-line arguments.

Injection does not save values in run configurations, create dotenv files, or use CLI fallback storage. Downloads fail rather than reuse stored secrets when Doppler is unavailable. Account and folder defaults are checked during loading to prevent injection after a detected account or config change.

Authentication is managed by the Doppler CLI through doppler login. The plugin does not store your authentication token. When account validation detects an account change or loss of authentication, affected cached secret documents are cleared.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ Platform 2025.3 (build 253) or later.
  • The Terminal plugin installed and enabled.
  • The Doppler CLI installed and authenticated.

Run and Debug integrations additionally require the corresponding IDE plugins: Java; Java and Maven for Maven configurations; Gradle; JavaScript and Node.js; Python; or Docker. These integrations are optional and depend on your IDE and edition. Browsing and editing secrets do not require the language or Docker plugins. Configure the relevant runtimes, build tools, and Docker tooling as you would for native Run configurations.
